The Factory Floor

A software factory as a live production line: tickets enter, agents build in parallel, automatic gates catch defects, a person approves, and changes ship. Move the sliders to see what limits the line: more agents, weaker gates or too few reviewers. Tap a station for what it does and what real companies report.

Tap a station

Each station explains its job, what usually goes wrong, and what published sources report about it.

How to read this

The line is a toy simulation with made-up rates: each agent makes 3 changes a day; badly specified tasks are more likely to carry a defect or be thrown away; gates catch a share of defects; reviewers catch 70% of what is left when not overloaded, less when the queue grows. It shows direction, not real outcomes. Real figures in the station panels come from Stripe’s Minions posts (Feb 2026), GitHub Octoverse 2026, LinearB’s 2026 benchmarks (vendor data ⚠️) and DORA 2025.

Read the series: 1. What a software factory is · 2. Stripe’s Minions · 3. Building the line · 4. Gates and measures · 5. Our factory and the road ahead.
